newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies rally for gains.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies rally for gains.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures turned higher after early weakness with hog futures pacing the advance on commercial demand, traders said.
December ran up 0.900 cent to 58.400 cents per lb at 1057 CST, the highest level since October 9. Other months were 0.700 cent higher to unchanged.

Spillover strength from cattle pits combined with commercial buying to offset early profit taking, traders said. Expectaions of stronger cash hog prices when all packing plants are back on line after the holiday Monday, provided much of the buying interest, sources said.
Rand Financials bought December, Rosenthal Collins bought February and Lind-Waldock was a buyer in April, pit sources said.
In hog options, Lind-Waldock sold December 54 calls and Merrill Lynch bought October 64 calls, pit sources added.

Pork belly futures turned up after early profit taking presure from a somewhat overbought condition, traders noted. Strength in livestock pits combined with recent strong fundamentals to turn prices higher, traders said.

A recently-reduced pace of hog slaughter, lighter-than- expected belly storings and higher cash belly prices added to fundamental support. Cash belly prices rose to $64 per cwt on Friday, the highest price level since October 14, they said.
At 1105 CST, pork bellies stood 0.100 cent a lb higher to 0.600 lower with only thinly traded back months lower. February was up most at 74.575 cents.
